reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers is amazing! He's very funny, keeps class engaging, and pokes fun in a nice way. He cold-calls two or three people per class, and he does his best to guide you toward the answer. His classes are extremely test-heavy, with three exams graded at 30% each. Be prepared for a lot of reading and getting used to the format he expects in class.

I took him for both 355 and 461 -- I would not recommend doing both at same time. LOTS of outside reading/theoretical understanding. Super interesting class but not an easy A by any means. Def be prepared for class to be cold called on for the entire lecture. He isn't super hard on you for the cold calls but he won't give you the answer either.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 exams and socratic participation. Not hard at all (usually you are going to law school if you are in this class) but he def pushes you. Not an easy A by any means but you will learn a lot. Lots of reading and the exams are written - Don't take if you don't want to do at least an hour of outside reading/work a day. Prof is very sarcastic
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course was only graded by a few things. Tests made up 90% of the grade, and the rest was participation, which was done through a socratic manner. Did not mind the participation. However, the tests were difficult and writing intensive. I did study for the course. However, if you're not ready to risk dropping your GPA a little, I wouldn't take it.

This is for 355, but that wasn't listed. Dr. Rogers is awesome. The class is set up for those who want to go to law school. Most days, you're assigned 2 cases and he cold calls students. You're graded on 3 tests and participation (if you were cold called, you could keep up with him). He is hilarious and truly cares about his students!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Class is set up like law school (afaik, everyone who takes this class wants to go to law school, so this is useful). He cold calls students to ask them about the cases he assigned that day, so you have to go to class. 90% of your grade is based on three exams. Classes are interactive, funny, and interesting

Rogers is one of my favorite professors in all of my college career. You can tell he is passionate about this material. The material he teaches isn't easy but he does his best to explain it. He is very understanding, wants his students to do well, and likes to tell funny stories. If you go to class you will do good.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class
